title: On Patmos (Revelation 1:9–20)
hook: John, exiled, sees the risen Christ among lampstands: fear not
carry: fear not, I am the first

segments.voice: Yesterday, Alpha and Omega: God holding the whole alphabet, A to Z. Your line was the beginning and the end. Looking back on the week, what sat in the messy middle? Day one thousand two hundred eighty-nine.

"I John, who also am your brother, and companion in tribulation." That's how the man who saw all this introduces himself. Not as a prophet, not as a bishop. Your brother. Your companion in the hard part. Then he says where he is: "in the isle that is called Patmos, for the word of God, and for the testimony of Jesus Christ." An island, sea on every side, and he's there, he says, for the word of God. Tradition says he'd been banished. It's the Lord's day. He's in the Spirit, and from behind him comes a voice loud as a trumpet. Today, the moment John turns around.
screen: `A VOICE LIKE A TRUMPET, BEHIND HIM.`

segments.voice: First, he turns to see a voice. That's how the King James puts it: "And I turned to see the voice that spake with me. And being turned, I saw seven golden candlesticks." Lampstands, standing in the dark. And in the midst of them, "one like unto the Son of man." Second, the figure. John piles up pictures, because ordinary words won't hold it. Hair white as wool, white as snow. Eyes like a flame of fire. Feet like polished brass glowing in a furnace. A voice like the sound of many waters. Seven stars in his right hand. A sharp two-edged sword coming from his mouth. A face like the sun at full strength. These aren't meant to be drawn like a photo; they're meant to overwhelm. Third, what John does, and what Christ does. "When I saw him, I fell at his feet as dead." And then the tender part: "he laid his right hand upon me, saying unto me, Fear not; I am the first and the last." The same right hand that holds the stars is laid on a frightened man. And he goes on: "I am he that liveth, and was dead; and, behold, I am alive for evermore." Fourth, the vision explains itself. Christ tells John what the lampstands are: "the seven candlesticks which thou sawest are the seven churches." So the first thing Revelation unveils about the risen Christ is where he stands. Not far off in the sky. In the midst of the churches, among the small, flickering lamps, with all their trouble. Present, not distant.

Here's the practice: hear fear not. Settle, and breathe. Name one thing you're afraid of at the moment, quietly, just to yourself. Don't argue with it. Then imagine a hand laid on you, warm and steady, as in the vision. If you pray, you can let the words come: Fear not; I am the first and the last. If you don't, just notice the steadiness of the hand. Each time the fear comes back, feel the hand again. The bell holds the time.
On Patmos. An island where John, companion in tribulation, saw the risen Christ standing among lampstands, and heard: fear not.
Your line: fear not, I am the first. Today, put a hand on someone's shoulder, or send a message that does the same, to someone who's afraid. Day one thousand two hundred eighty-nine.

howItsDone: Christians read this vision of the risen Christ in personal prayer and in church, and its words 'fear not; I am the first and the last' are read in times of grief and trouble.

notes: Exile: the text says John was on Patmos 'for the word of God, and for the testimony of Jesus Christ'; banishment is given as 'tradition says'. Confirm.
'It's the Lord's day' — Rev 1:10; kept as written, not glossed as Sunday.
Description of the figure (1:14–16) paraphrased; check each image.
KJV 'candlesticks' glossed as lampstands in the voice.

Editor pass: 'small island' and 'because of what he preached' brought back to the text ('for the word of God'); the text says the hand was laid 'upon me', not on his shoulder, so 'shoulder' is cut; removed the stock 'you're not standing alone' line from the practice.
Audit (1282–1291): fork setup said John was 'praying'; the text says he was 'in the Spirit on the Lord's day' (1:10), so the setup now follows the text. Rev 1:9–20 quotations checked against KJV.
